newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dlr up as trade row fears fade,stocks mixed.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dlr up as trade row fears fade,stocks mixed.

text.p: The dollar climbed half a yen as President Bill Clinton helped to calm worries that a summit of the leading industrial nations starting on Friday would become a forum for a U.S.-Japan trade row.
European bourses were mixed despite a buoyant overnight finish on Wall Street. Frankfurt made big gains, helped by the dollar, but London made an unsteady showing.

The U.S. currency strengthened against then yen as world leaders gathered for the three-day meeting of the Group of Seven (G7) in Denver. Remarks by Clinton helped to kill market talk that Washington would criticise Tokyo because of the recent jump in its trade surplus.
Clinton said he was concerned about Japan's large trade surplus with the United States but added that Tokyo was taking steps to boost domestic demand.

Exchange rates are a touchy issue in Japanese-American relations because a strong dollar helps Tokyo's exports of cars and other goods to the United States. But Clinton added that exchange rates should not be used to correct trade balances.

Traders took this as reassurance that Washington would not resort to calls for a weaker dollar to help to redress the trade imbalance, as it has done in the past. But they were wary of pushing the dollar aggressively higher until after the G7.

"Trade will play some role in the G7 discussions, which might see the yen a touch firmer next week," said Steven Hannah, the director of economic research at IBJ International. "But I don't expect it to be too big an issue given that Clinton has already made it clear that talking the dollar down is not the appropriate way to deal with the problem."

The dollar was quoted at 114.62 yen, compared with 114.09 in late trade on Thursday. Concern that Denver would become the setting for a row had driven the dollar down as low as 112.75 earlier this week.

A long rally by the dollar reached a four-and-a-half year high of 127.46 yen on May 1. But traders largely ignored the two G7 summits earlier this year calling for an end to its climb and for more currency stability.

The dollar is expected to make less headway in the wake of this summit, given that the trade concerns will linger until Japan's trade surplus, particularly with the United States, show signs of narrowing.
The stronger dollar helped boost European bourses. Frankfurt climbed 1.25 percent at one to stage to hit an intra-day high of 3,798.94 points on the 30-share DAX index in busy trading.

"It looks like today is going to be rather volatile but in the end we should see modest gains for the day," said one head trader at a Stuttgart-based bank. "There's no real end in sight to this rally."
Frankfurt investors were encouraged by the dollar. "The market is more focused on the U.S. right now instead of on domestic factors," said one trader.
London, Europe's biggest bourse, flitted in and out of profit in volatile trade with investors focusing on the mid-morning expiry of index options, seen as a negative factor overhanging the market.
After the expiry, the FTSE 100 index of leading shares showed its relief by heading for higher ground but slipped back again by lunch time.

London, which has fallen 140 points in the past week, has been dogged by worries of higher interest rates and fears the new Labour government's first budget on July 2 will contain bad news for investors.
The market has been unsettled by persistent press reports that finance minister Gordon Brown will scrap a tax break on dividend payments to major corporate investors.
In Paris, stocks made useful gains but trade was thin with investors digesting the implications of Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's first major policy address on Thursday.

"There's not a lot of interest or a lot of volume," a broker said. "Although we were expecting some clarifications, a lot of doubt remains. A lot of decisions have been put off to September so uncertainty persists."
CURRENCIES AT 1200 GMT
The dollar was at 1.7273 marks and 114.62 yen, compared with 1.7247 and 114.09 in late European trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1200 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 3.5 points at 4,650.2.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 16.47 points at 2,756.16.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 39.00 at 3788.27.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $339.55 against $339.75 on Thursday. Silver was barely changed at $4.76.
